card.title: Remember What I Meant
card.instruction: Create openings for shared memories that prove your past presence mattered and still deserves acknowledgment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's my sleeve in your graduation photo.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You caught me when I tripped.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Funny how the sleeve made the official album.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I remember the person in it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell me that bit. The sleeve's heard enough.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 points out a trace of A in the photo, A3 keeps the shared rescue in view, and A5 asks B to tell the remembered person's part.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's caught-me memory informs A3's sleeve-in-album remark; B4's personal recognition enables A5's request to hear that memory.

relationship.evidence: B2 remembers the actual help and B4 warmly distinguishes the person from the visible sleeve.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's recognition to invite a fuller acknowledgment; the heightening remains intimate and small.

specificity.evidence: A1-B2 establish a graduation photo and a caught stumble.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's sleeve-has-heard-enough follows B4's person-versus-sleeve distinction.

coach2.missing: No essential gap about the fall or relationship label is required.
coach2.firstDefect: No mandatory defect; A creates and sustains an opening for acknowledgment of past presence.
